Committee: Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development
Sponsor: Orr
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 02/03/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 76 as introduced could increase the administrative obligations of state agencies and county or municipal governing bodies responsible for administering permits for the installation of small wireless facilities on public utility infrastructure (right-of-way). Any increase in obligations would be offset by permit fees, ranging from $250 to $1,000 depending on the type of installment, and the rate charged for access to right-of-ways, not to exceed $170, pursuant to the provisions of this bill.
Steve Livingston, Chairperson
Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development

Senate Bill 76 as introduced and as amended and reported by the Committee on Fiscal Responsibility and Economic Development could increase the administrative obligations of state agencies and county or municipal governing bodies responsible for administering permits for the installation of small wireless facilities on public utility infrastructure (right-of-way). Committee: Urban and Rural Development
Sponsor: Orr
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 02/05/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 76 as passed the Senate could increase the administrative obligations of state agencies and county or municipal governing bodies responsible for administering permits for the installation of small wireless facilities on public utility infrastructure (right-of-way). Any increase in obligations would be offset, at least in part, by (1) one-time permit fees, ranging from $250 to $1,000 depending on the type of installment, and (2) the rate charged for access to right-of-ways, not to exceed $170 annually, pursuant to the provisions of this bill.
Randall Shedd, Chair
Urban and Rural Development

Committee: Finance and Taxation Education
Sponsor: Chesteen
Analyst: John Friedenreich
Date: 04/20/2021
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 351 as introduced would reduce receipts to the Education Trust Fund (ETF) by an estimated $3.96 million annually, beginning in FY 2023, to allow individuals serving on active duty that claim Alabama as their state of legal residence, but not residing in the state to claim an income tax deduction for their active duty military pay. The loss in ETF receipts each year would depend on the number of active duty military personnel claiming this deduction and providing an annual certification of residence status to the Alabama Department of Revenue.
As substituted and reported by the Committee on Finance and Taxation Education, would reduce receipts to the Education Trust Fund (ETF) by an estimated $2.56 million annually, and would allow individuals serving on active duty that claim Alabama as their state of legal residence but are stationed or deployed outside the 50 states of the United States and the District of Columbia to claim an income tax deduction for their active duty military pay.
Arthur Orr, Chairperson
Finance and Taxation Education
